authority: User answer in the 2026-11-26 session after campaign-2: 'Raise cap, re-run Ne/Ar'.
revises: the Ne and Ar application decks generated by prepare_atomic_pilot_cases.py (tracing_maximum_substep_s only); the approval record and the first revision are otherwise unchanged
rule: tracing_maximum_substep_s equals the coarsest common step (horizon / 8) in every case. He already satisfies it (65536 / 8 = 8192), so the He decks are unchanged.
reason: Campaign-2 (test_output/srcMoon/i22-atomic-pilot-C7b2SG5d/campaign-2/, retained) passed every He check. Ne and Ar failed only the strict-decrease event-time refinement check, with errors flat at about 1.5e-15 of the horizon at 8, 16 and 32 steps. The decks inherit tracing_maximum_substep_s = 8192 from the I21 compact deck, and the production photon history (TrajectoryExposure::BuildPhotonHistory) is built over each mover substep with linear interpolation of the (AU/r)^2 factor. Every Ne and Ar common step is at least 8192 s, so the refinement left the exposure grid unchanged. The independent prediction of the interpolation error over 8192 s, h^2 * 6 (v/r)^2 / 12 with v = 1 m/s and r = 1.4689e11 m, is 1.56e-15, which matches the observed plateau; the He errors fall 4x per halving as predicted. The earlier description of this plateau as an arithmetic floor was wrong.
precedent: The I23 and I24 PIC runners set tracing_maximum_substep_s to the step; the I21 decision-1 gravity decks use 16384.
